editorial:
You follow three estranged brothers as they board a colorful train across India, hoping a spiritual trip will fix their broken bond. Francis, Peter, and Jack bring old wounds, secrets, and a lot of luggage, both real and emotional. The trip quickly turns messy with painkillers, cough syrup, and pepper spray, but that chaos is part of the charm. The movie mixes dry humor, warm family tension, and beautiful travel scenes into a story that feels both funny and sad.

The cast makes the brothers feel real, and the bright visuals keep every stop interesting. The pacing can feel slow if you want nonstop action, and the quirky style may not be for everyone. Still, the emotional payoff lands well. If you enjoy character-driven road trips, watch it streaming in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the brothers miss their train and sprint after it, dropping their father's heavy luggage along the way. That choice shows they are finally letting go of old grief and choosing each other. Their mother stays distant at the convent, but the brothers leave together, bruised yet closer, with the train carrying them forward as a family again.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves character-driven road trips and offbeat family stories.
